A stronger traditional: labs that share inside, on a graph where deeper ideas are much harder (4 bits per level)

Question: On a graph where deeper ideas are much harder (4 bits per level), how much money do traditional labs that share inside the lab need, against OSO?

Answer: At budget 32: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Design (fixed before the run): compared traditional with agents alone or in labs (2 of 6, 3 of 4, one of 9, one of 12) against OSO at α = 0.8 and 0.2, by budget · held the same: a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7), 12 identical agents, budget 75 split equally, no mint, no validation · measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste · 30 graphs × 5 runs on each, per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

The simple model on a graph where deeper ideas are much harder (4 bits per level), 6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, composition 0.7; each graph run 5 times. Traditional rules (α = 1, nothing published before a target), with the 12 agents alone, in 2 labs of 6, in 3 labs of 4, in one lab of 9 with 3 alone, or in one lab of all 12; lab mates share every proof at once, privately. Money is equal per agent, so a bigger lab has more. Against OSO at α = 0.8 and 0.2. Held fixed: 12 identical agents, equal money every round (f = 0), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, no validation.

Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
